questions.prompt: Which core feature is the best one to build first?
choices: The colour-coded output, because it is what people notice
Adding a task and printing the list, because it is the smallest thing that works end to end
All four core features at once, so they fit together properly
The one you find hardest, to get it over with
questions.explain: Something small that runs end to end gives you a program you can re-run after every change. Building four at once means that the first time you run it, four things can be wrong.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of building one feature in order.
items: Write the function for one core feature
Run it and check it does what you meant
Move on to the next core feature
Come back and tidy the structure once several features exist
questions.explain: Checking before moving on is what keeps a bug attached to the change that caused it. Tidying comes later, when there is enough code to see the shape of.

questions.prompt: When is it worth pulling a working block of code out into its own function?
choices: Whenever it is more than five lines long
When you need the same behaviour somewhere else, or when you want to give the block a name
Never, since more functions means more to read
Only when someone asks you to
questions.explain: Reuse and naming are the two reasons that pay. Line count is not one: a long function doing one thing is fine, and a three-line function used twice is worth extracting.

questions.prompt: Which of these mean a feature is core rather than nice-to-have?
choices: The project does not do its main job without it
It is named in the purpose section of your proposal
It would look impressive in a demo
Other planned features depend on it
questions.explain: Core is decided by whether the project works without it. Impressive is a reason to build something once the core is done.

reflection-exercise1.hint: A core feature is one the project is pointless without. Say which of yours are core and why the rest can wait.

reflection-exercise2.hint: Smallest thing that works, then check it, then the next. Say where functions come in as the project grows.
